_readme: Manifest for tools/wcet.py — the machine-checkable half of budget
contract clause C-3. Every entry here is a CLAIM about the code that CI
re-checks on every build. `loops` is the number of cycles (strongly
connected components, reducible or not) the compiler emitted for that
function: it is deliberately brittle, because a change to it means the
loop structure of the audio ISR changed and a human must look. Bounds are
read out of each loop's own `cmp rN,#imm` exit test where one exists (see
infer_bound); `default_bound` covers the rest and needs the justification
in `why`. A loop with no edge leaving its body is rejected outright.
_sdram_note: These are the out-of-line readers of the external delay buffer; their
loads are priced at SDRAM_LOAD rather than SRAM. SDRAM traffic that the
compiler INLINED into bsp_audio_isr (dl_write, pt_read/pt_write, the
overdub read-modify-write) is still priced as SRAM — the model cannot
tell which pointer an inlined load followed. That underestimate is one of
the things the calibration ratio K absorbs; it is also why the ratio
between builds, not the absolute ceiling, is the regression signal.

_note: K = measured worst-case cycles / modelled ceiling, recorded with
--calibrate <isr_pk>. The ceiling assumes the most expensive branch
everywhere at once, so it is larger than any single real path; K says
by how much, for a build whose real load is known.
PROVENANCE of this value: the measurement is the lead's, isr_pk 4104 =
117% of budget in TIME/RECIRC with a loop playing, taken on the image
BEFORE workstream B's changes; the ceiling it is divided by is the
image AFTER them, because that is the one this tool can disassemble.
The two differ, so treat this K as an anchor of the right order and
re-record it next time the unit is on the bench: build, flash, reset
g_isr_pk, run the WCC-TIME programme, read isr_pk back, then

0.why: Single-block loop = the varispeed write burst `while (lp_phase >= 1.0f) { advance; lp_phase -= 1; }`. lp_phase gains lp_rate per input sample and lp_rate is clamped to 4.0 in engine.c, so it can never carry more than 4 whole samples plus the sub-sample remainder: 5 iterations is the construction bound. Four copies exist (overdub and plain paths, each specialised twice).

1.why: as loop 0 — varispeed write burst, bounded by the 0.25..4.0 rate clamp

2.why: as loop 0 — varispeed write burst, bounded by the 0.25..4.0 rate clamp

3.why: as loop 0 — varispeed write burst, bounded by the 0.25..4.0 rate clamp

9.why: The frame loop = BLOCK_FRAMES. It contains the entire per-sample engine, so it is the one loop whose bound has to be exact rather than defaulted.

bsp_audio_isr.why: Ten loops, in three classes, and the class is legible from the body size. (a) Four SINGLE-BLOCK loops = the varispeed/overdub write bursts, bounded at 5 by the rate clamp — see the overrides. (b) Five MEDIUM loops (11-26 blocks) = the per-tap / per-slot / per-string work that the compiler inlined into the frame loop: the 8-tap read, the declick and mixer passes, the pitch echo pattern (7), the 8-slot output conversion, the KS string bank (8), the splice chunk (SPLICE_CHUNK 8). Every one of those iterates over NUM_TAPS, TDM_SLOTS, KS_STRINGS or SPLICE_CHUNK, all of which are 8, so 8 is the default and it is a bound, not a guess. The heavier 16- and 32-iteration work (the AA polyphase FIR over AA_TAPS, its streaming-cache refill) is NOT here: it lives out of line in ps_read_bl, which is bounded separately. If a future change inlines that into the ISR, the loop COUNT above changes and the build fails until someone re-justifies this paragraph — which is exactly what should happen. (c) The 383-block loop is the frame loop; see the override.

dl_read_loop_frac.why: Loop-free for the same reason: the loop-window mapping is conditional arithmetic, not a normalisation loop.

ps_read_bl.why: The polyphase FIR accumulation over AA_TAPS = 16 coefficients.

read_frac_at_index.why: Loop-free, and worth stating explicitly: the `while (r < 0) r += len` / `while (r >= len) r -= len` normalisation loops live in dl_read_at(), the FLOAT-index read, which the audio path does not call. The exact int+frac path the engine actually uses wraps with conditional adds. If a future change routes the ISR through dl_read_at, this count changes and the build fails — which is the point, because those loops are bounded only by a caller invariant (position within a buffer length of the range), not by construction.
